description:
Quinqui is a Spanish subculture and social identity that emerged in the late 1970s and 1980s during the Spanish transition to democracy era. [ 1 ] It originated in the marginalized working-class suburbs ( extrarradios ) of major cities like Madrid, Barcelona, and Bilbao. The term "Quinqui" is derived from quincallero , referring to nomadic groups who traditionally traded in scrap metal or cheap items ( quincalla ). The term merchero holds the same meaning, even when some mercheros distance themselves from the term "Quinqui".

The aesthetic is a lived reality of poverty and survival that was later popularized and romanticized by a specific film genre known as "Cine Quinqui." It is the essential origin aesthetic for modern Spanish working-class street styles, such as Bakala , Pokero , Cani , Raxet , and MDLR .
culturalContext: Key values (per the Aesthetics Wiki): Survival, "living fast," delinquency as rebellion, loyalty to the neighborhood (el barrio)
